title: Hollow anchors at the first build commit when no BUILDME crossing is journaled
intention: cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py's build_anchor anchors a ticket whose journals hold no forward crossing into BUILDME at the parent of its first build commit, instead of refusing; a ticket with neither a forward BUILDME crossing nor a build commit is still refused, by name.
why: Measured 2026-10-12 on 4ddc9df3369e: its BUILDME stood by a 09-07 PROVEME->BUILDME back-edge and its only forward crossing into BUILDME predates the journals (journals start 2026-09-06), so 'cairn test --hollow 4ddc9df3369e --seal' refused HollowUnmeasurable ('no journal in either root records a forward crossing into BUILDME') over a build committed as 3024a302 '4ddc9df3369e: build', and the PROVED rung bounced the boat to FIXME on hollow_evidence_absent. By hand at n=1 in a scratch worktree with a scratch commons beside it, trouble.py reverted to 6de07e69 redded, node_classes/trouble.json removed redded, both restored greened: the build is measurable and the instrument could not say so. Trouble hollow-has-no-baseline-when-buildme-predates-the-journals. The peer (akiendelllinux_cc_0, 2026-10-12) ruled option (a), this ticket, and rejected (b), flipping the live trouble store to re-measure ('reseal-storms ~100 proofs to measure one ticket'). Pre-approved through PROVED under Akien's 2026-10-12 words: 'anything that just needs approved is approved ... APPROVED THRU PROVED. FASTEST ROUTE TO EVERYTHING PROVED SO WE CAN DO THE DETAILED REVIEW.'
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass: the reading must be takeable for a build that is measurable) and Law 3 (an unmeasured claim is labeled: a ticket with no anchor is still refused by name).
how: cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py only. (1) WHEN: build_anchor calls crossings.buildme_crossing(tid, roots) directly; the fallback runs ONLY when it returns None, i.e. no forward crossing into BUILDME exists in the journals at all. This is the reading of 'no forward BUILDME crossing' the peer confirmed 2026-10-12; a literal 'no crossing after the first build commit' would switch nearly every ticket onto the fallback, because the normal order is crossing first, build commit after. When a forward crossing exists the existing rule runs byte-for-byte unchanged. (2) BUILD COMMITS: a new _anchor_without_a_crossing(ticket, files, *, roots, repo_root, instrument, read_by) gathers, on HEAD, the union of (a) every commit whose subject starts '<tid>: build' and (b) the commits _build_commits already returns (message names tid and changes a measured writes_to file), deduped, oldest first by committer time. The latest back-edge bound is computed exactly as build_anchor computes it (factor the 'backs'/'bound' block into a helper _bound(tid, roots, builds) both call), and only build commits after the bound count. (3) ANCHOR: the parent of the first of those; every other counted build commit must descend from it (merge-base --is-ancestor), else HollowUnmeasurable naming the commit that does not. The return carries commit, anchor_rule 'first-build-commit-no-crossing', anchor_journal None, anchor_first_build, anchor_first_build_parent, buildme_at None, bound, and build_commits (the counted shas). The measured file set stays writes_to (the chart's claim, per the writes_to docstring); every file any counted build commit wrote is pre-build at the anchor because the anchor precedes them all, so a later build commit cannot hide. (4) REFUSAL: no counted build commit raises HollowUnmeasurable whose text names both lacks: no journal records a forward crossing into BUILDME for the ticket, and no '<tid>: build' commit (nor a commit naming the ticket that changes a measured writes_to file) exists after the bound. The word BUILDME stays in the text (test_hollow.py tooth test_a_run_that_could_not_be_measured_says_so_instead_of_passing reads it). No commit at the parent (a root commit) also refuses, naming it. (5) measure()'s postdates-the-build message reads (anchor['anchor_journal'] or 'none')[:12]. The commons anchor (build_anchor called with repo_root=commons) goes through the same code, unchanged. The module docstring gains one paragraph citing this ticket and the 4ddc measurement. Nothing outside hollow.py changes (RULE 1).
falsifier: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow_anchors_without_a_journaled_buildme.py under PROVES {'f8d58aff88f9': {'1','2','3'}}, scratch repo + commons + berth store per the fixture in cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow_anchors_before_the_build_that_stands.py: (1) commits c0 (VALUE=1, unrelated), '<id>: build' (VALUE=2), '<id>: build more' (VALUE=2), journal holding only BUILDME->PROVEME forward and PROVEME->FIXME back: measure returns commit == c0, anchor_rule 'first-build-commit-no-crossing', and subject.py reds the fixture tooth; (2) c0, a forward TICKETME->BUILDME crossing, an unrelated commit u, then '<id>: build': measure returns commit == c0 with anchor_rule 'journal' (the fallback would pick u), exactly as today; (3) no commit naming the ticket and no forward BUILDME crossing: HollowUnmeasurable whose text contains 'BUILDME' and '<id>: build'. Hollow: reverting hollow.py reds 1 (refuses) and 3 (the text names no build commit). Live: after PROVED, 'cairn test --hollow 4ddc9df3369e' is not refused for want of an anchor.
